claims.text: A finer, dynamically amorphized near-surface structure in a FeNiCrCoCu coating will improve wear resistance during high-temperature sliding.
Near-surface refinement and amorphization will shift deformation from dislocation-dominated mechanisms to grain-boundary-mediated processes.
Standard deposition produces a moderately coarse- to fine-grained FeNiCrCoCu coating.
A higher-heat-input process or annealing treatment can promote near-surface dynamic recrystallization or amorphization relative to the baseline coating.
Elevated-temperature sliding activates dynamic evolution of the near-surface microstructure.
Above an unspecified temperature threshold, grain-boundary sliding becomes significant in FeNiCrCoCu.
A controlled or inert atmosphere mitigates oxidation during sliding.
The modified coating will form an ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface layer.
The ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface layer will exhibit inverse Hall-Petch behavior.
The refined and possibly amorphous nanostructure increases the contribution of grain-boundary sliding.
The refined and possibly amorphous nanostructure dynamically accommodates sliding strain.
Formation of an ultra-nanocrystalline or dynamically amorphized near-surface layer reduces friction.
Formation of an ultra-nanocrystalline or dynamically amorphized near-surface layer reduces wear.
The modified FeNiCrCoCu coating will have a lower wear rate than the baseline coating during high-temperature sliding.
The modified coating will show more evidence of grain-boundary sliding than the baseline.
The modified coating will show more dynamic amorphization than the baseline during sliding.
The predicted behavior is restricted to elevated-temperature sliding regimes in which dynamic grain refinement is activated and excessive oxidation is limited.
